Manila Ordinance:
The Manila Ordinance lists four exemptions: minors accompanied by parents or legal-age family members/guardians; those running lawful errands; night school students and employed minors out after 10 PM; and night workers.
The Manila Ordinance imposes various sanctions on minors based on age and frequency of violations:
For offenders 15 years of age and below, the sanction is a reprimand for the youth offender and admonition to the offender's parent, guardian or person exercising parental authority.
For offenders between 15 and 18 years of age, the sanction is:
Reprimand and Admonition for the first offense.
Reprimand and Admonition, and a warning about the legal impostitions in case of a third and subsequent violation for the second offense.
Imprisonment of one (1) day to ten (10) days, or a Fine of TWO THOUSAND PESOS (Php2,000.00), or both at the discretion of the Court, for the THIRD AND SUBSEQUENT OFFENSES.
Navotas Ordinance:
The Navotas Ordinance provides more exceptions: minors with night classes; night workers; those attending school or church activities (coordinated with a barangay office); those traveling home during curfew hours; those running errands under parental supervision; those involved in accidents/calamities.
The Navotas Ordinance exempts minors on Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year's Eve, New Year's Day, the night before the barangay fiesta, the day of the fiesta, All Saints' and All Souls' Day, Holy Thursday, Good Friday, Black Saturday, and Easter Sunday.
This Ordinance required community service in lieu of fines if parents were unable to pay.
Quezon City Ordinance:
The Quezon City Ordinance provides the following exceptions:
Those accompanied by their parents or guardian;
Those on their way to or from a party, graduation ceremony, religious mass, and/or other extra-curricular activities of their school or organization wherein their attendance are required or otherwise indispensable, or when such minors are out and unable to go home early due to circumstances beyond their control as verified by the proper authorities concerned; and
Those attending to, or in experience of, an emergency situation such as conflagration, earthquake, hospitalization, road accident, law enforcers encounter, and similar incidents[;]
When the minor is engaged in an authorized employment activity, or going to or returning home from the same place of employment activity without any detour or stop;
When the minor is in [a] motor vehicle or other travel accompanied by an adult in no violation of this Ordinance;
When the minor is involved in an emergency;
When the minor is out of his/her residence attending an official school, religious, recreational, educational, social, community or other similar private activity sponsored by the city, barangay, school, or other similar private civic/religious organization/group (recognized by the community) that supervises the activity or when the minor is going to or returning home from such activity, without any detour or stop; and
When the minor can present papers certifying that he/she is a student and was dismissed from his/her class/es in the evening or that he/she is a working student.
Outcome:
The Manila and Navotas Ordinances were declared unconstitutional.
The Quezon City Ordinance was declared constitutional.
